summary: Removed the unsupported freshness superlative flagged in Director review: src/content/blog/beginner/life-line.md no longer calls Lucas et al. (2019) 'the most recent peer-reviewed study'; the empirical paragraph now lists the three verified studies (Newrick et al. 1990 significant association, Wilson & Mather 1974 no correlation, Lucas et al. 2019 no correlation) without a freshness ranking and closes with 'across these three published studies, the record is mixed and does not establish a reliable predictive relationship,' scoping the conclusion explicitly to the verified record rather than a general claim. Also reworded the two nearby summary sentences that said 'the studies that have tested it find no reliable relationship' (life-line.md's FAQ answer and 04-life-line.mdx's closing Lesson takeaway) to 'the limited published studies that have tested it show a mixed record that does not establish a reliable relationship,' so neither can be misread as claiming all three studies were negative. 04-life-line.mdx line 28 (the earlier 'myth, corrected' section) contains the same construction but was left unchanged as outside the authorized scope (only the empirical/testing discussion in life-line.md and the closing takeaway in 04-life-line.mdx were authorized); flagged as a candidate for a future bounded pass. No new studies, citations, palmistry interpretations, or scientific claims were introduced; the three verified citations and outcomes from Pass 6 are unchanged. Added Pass 7 to docs/source-verification-log.md documenting this correction and updated docs/CURRENT_STATE.md's PP-RELAY-024 paragraph, which quoted the revision-1 wording that changed. Pushed to the existing claude/relay-PP-RELAY-024-life-line-sourcing branch and updated PR #40's footer to revision 2.
